expectations.text: The response rejects day-of 'ask a volunteer' dietary handling, requiring restrictions collected before the event so the catering order is adjusted in advance rather than improvised on the day.
expectations.evidence: '"allergies? ask a volunteer" is not a plan'; 'Ask everyone who will be fed before the event.'

expectations.text: The dietary ask covers everyone who will be fed - participants, mentors, volunteers, and staff - not attendees alone.
expectations.evidence: 'all ~340 people: participants, mentors and volunteers.'

expectations.text: It names the restriction categories to ask about: vegetarian, vegan, celiac and gluten-free, common allergies with lactose and peanut named, kosher, and halal.
expectations.evidence: Lists gluten-free, celiac, diabetes, and allergens, with 'religious or cultural diets' as a group. Vegetarian, vegan, kosher and halal are never named.

expectations.text: It gives the two fallback paths when the supplier cannot cover a restriction: a one-off request to the existing supplier for a small number of prepared meals, or a delivery credit given to the attendee with advance notice so they can plan.
expectations.evidence: 'ask for a one-off adjustment to the order'; 'give that person a delivery credit with advance notice'.

expectations.text: It includes the distribution safeguard: restricted meals held at a separate table with names checked off a printed list as meals are handed out.
expectations.evidence: 'Hold restricted meals at a separate table. Check names off a printed list'.

expectations.text: It presents this dietary practice as one organization's published practice, not an industry norm.
expectations.evidence: Cites '[sourced] from the hackathon organizer guide and the IACC dietary guide' but never frames it as not being an industry norm.

expectations.text: It routes the final dietary commitment into the catering brief through the vendor or catering function rather than leaving it informal.
expectations.evidence: 'Send the results to the caterer now.'

expectations.text: It corrects the sticker meanings to interaction-consent signals: green open to talk, yellow only if you know me, red not interested in talking - not personality or extrovert/introvert labels.
expectations.evidence: 'Green: open to talk. Yellow: only if you know me. Red: not interested in talking...' replacing the extrovert/introvert framing.

expectations.text: It states that red also signals not wanting to be photographed or filmed - one artifact carrying both a social boundary and a recording opt-out.
expectations.evidence: 'Red: not interested in talking, or in being photographed or filmed.'

expectations.text: It routes enforcement (someone photographing or recording a red-sticker wearer) to the code of conduct's incident process rather than drafting consequences itself.
expectations.evidence: 'The skill hands enforcement to `event-code-of-conduct`; it does not draft it.'

expectations.text: It rejects skipping the opening announcement, requiring roughly sixty seconds naming what exists and where, because a provision nobody announces is used only by people who already knew about it.
expectations.evidence: 'Spend about sixty seconds... a provision nobody announces is used only by the people who already knew about it.'

expectations.text: It requires the registration or help desk briefed on every provision, including any location deliberately kept off the website.
expectations.evidence: 'a briefing for the registration desk... Brief volunteers on every provision, including where each thing is.'

expectations.text: It requires walk-up provisions physically signposted, because anything that requires asking a human filters out the people least willing to ask.
expectations.evidence: 'back it up with physical signs'; 'Anything that requires asking a human filters out the people...'
